shortName: Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences at the University at Buffalo
additionalCoursework:
We strongly recommend you take a statistics course as well as courses in biochemistry, genetics and molecular biology.

We recommend that you take four courses in the social sciences and two additional humanities courses.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
We recruit students who appreciate and learn from each other's disparate experiences. Our program immerses you in an environment of broadly diverse perspectives where you will develop into a culturally competent physician who is better prepared to serve a variety of patient populations and collaborate with physicians from differing backgrounds.

Our diverse student and faculty population contributes to an encouraging, open-minded learning setting where you feel supported and included. We offer several enrichment programs for individuals from groups underrepresented in medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Student organizations form an integral part of campus life, serving the interests of our medical students and the greater community as well. Our student groups support a wide range of interests, including the American Medical Association Medical Student Section, Lighthouse Free Medical Clinic, Student National Medical Association and more.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Buffalo is characterized by a neighborly way of life, an unpretentious nature and spirited loyalty among residents. You will be captivated by Buffalo's beauty, heritage, temperate climate and welcoming environment. Buffalo offers plenty to do, with four-season recreation and affordable housing. Our Medical School is located downtown on the Buffalo-Niagara Medical Campus, a consortium of the region's innovative health care, education and research institutions.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: While on-campus housing is not available, the University maintains a list of affordable apartments and homes within a 10-mile radius of the campus. Rent averages $800-$1000 per month.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
The University at Buffalo is committed to ensuring a welcoming and safe environment for all members of our community, including our LGBTQ+ students, faculty, staff and community members.  The Office of Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) provides support, information and assistance.  

Our medical students partner with the Medical Student Pride Alliance (MSPA) as well as connect through OUTpatient. OUTpatient is the medical student LGBTQ+ alliance at Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences. The group works to improve the relationship between the LGBTQ+ community and health care professionals, as well as creating a sense of community among LGBTQ+ Medical Students and Physicians.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Jacobs School of Medicine has a Student Wellness Committee that was established to promote healthy lifestyle choices among medical students while raising awareness about the range of health and wellness services available at the University at Buffalo.
The group hosts lectures and workshops that address all aspect of wellness, including nutrition, finances, relationships, sleep and exercise.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: On a case by case basis.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: An orientation program is required of incoming students.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Our innovative and transformational Well Beyond Curriculum emphasizes structured support for students to foster personal and professional growth. Throughout their education at the Jacobs School, students are guided by dedicated faculty coaches in Learning Communities.  In the Case-Based Inquiry Learning program, small groups work closely with faculty facilitators to dissect patient cases, integrating foundational science with clinical diagnosis and treatment using a holistic approach. Our Educational Success Program helps students develop essential study skills to maximize success in medical school and beyond.

With a strong emphasis on early and enhanced clinical experiences, students engage in diverse health care environments from the outset, applying their learning to real-world scenarios throughout the 15 months of Phase 1. During the yearlong Phase 2, students care for patients through integrated clerkships in various clinical settings. Our expanded 14-month Phase 3 provides ample time for career exploration, residency preparation, and advanced clinical roles.
Community engagement is woven into the fabric of our curriculum. Throughout Phase 1, students will participate in meaningful service-learning with community organizations, building lasting relationships and understanding the social context of health care.

We integrate five core pillars into all courses and clerkships: foundational sciences, clinical sciences, health systems science, medical humanities, and scientific literacy and inquiry. This comprehensive approach ensures a well-rounded and transformative education.

Our students will become discerning consumers of medical literature and creators of new knowledge through an investigative inquiry course and participation in a scholarly health sciences project. And with a focus on systems-based practice, our graduates emerge equipped to excel within interdisciplinary teams and navigate the complexities of the modern and future health care landscape.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
You will have opportunities to engage in innovative clinical, basic and translational research with world-class faculty whose work contributes to important advances in a range of scientific and medical fields.

Research facilities in our building, from the basic science laboratories to the School's core facilities, were designed to promote collaboration between and among groups with varying expertise.

Our major research facility, UB's Clinical and Translational Research Center (CTRC), brings together physicians, researchers and medical students in a collaborative setting to bridge the gap between basic scientific research and clinical care for patients.
  
Our CTRC houses the laboratories of some of our highest-profile researchers, who collectively have more than $25 million in research funding. Our cutting-edge facility synthesizes the clinical and preclinical aspects of translational research and exposes you to innovative therapies and studies.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: We are strong advocates of service learning and encourage service in the local community.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Our medical students rotate among a variety of teaching sites. At Jacobs School you will work with urban, suburban and rural patient populations during your medical training.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Pass / Fail for the first 2 years.
Honors, High Satisfactory, Satisfactory, and Unsatisfactory for the last 2 clinical years.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Our goal is to prepare you so that you are capable of entering any field of graduate medical education and can excel in any field of medicine that currently exists or is likely to develop in the future.

We will help you develop the knowledge, ethics, clinical expertise and interpersonal skills you will need to become a successful, well-rounded physician. We emphasize both medical education and the basic sciences as underpinnings for the practice of medicine. Our wide range of clinical training experiences, research opportunities as well as our focus on medical humanities will complement our new Well Beyond Medical curriculum.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: We strive to advance health and wellness across the lifespan for the people of New York and the world by educating tomorrow's leaders in medicine and biomedical sciences that are capable of conducting innovative research and delivering outstanding clinical care.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Additional letters from physicians or supervisors in an employment capacity should speak to the applicant's attributes as delineated in our admissions policy.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Preference is from Pre-Health Committee if available. If undergraduate institution does not provide pre-health letter, three letters of recommendation with at least one letter from a science professor is required.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: We offer both in-person and virtual interviews to selected candidates. In person interviews held from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Wednesdays from August to March. Virtual interviews have been held at the convenience of interviewers and applicants. *The Jacobs School has no preference as to whether an applicant chooses to interview in person or virtually.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Yes. See information about interview day.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: EDP Candidates should only apply if their candidacy is highly competitive compared to other applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Apply if you have a competitive application
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Financial Aid may not be available.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
** Response to COVID-19 - Information **

Online Courses:  Our admissions policy explicitly states that prerequisite courses should be completed in a classroom setting and that laboratory coursework must be completed in an actual - not virtual or online - setting.  Due to limitations Covid presented in Schools across the country, the Jacobs School will accept online coursework from 2020 - 2021.

Pass/Fail Grades:  The Admissions Committee prefers that grades for prerequisite coursework be letter graded.  According to AAMC, two thirds of undergraduate schools adopted variations of a pass/fail grading system for the spring semester of 2020; therefore, we will accept pass/fail grades without prejudice for this semester.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: The Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences at the University at Buffalo employs a mission-aligned review process. In addition to upward transfer, accelerated and supplemental pathways, community college coursework will be evaluated and assessed within the context of the applicant’s other attributes and experiences.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Updated information is welcome. Information with instructions is available on our website.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The University at Buffalo, including the Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences (Jacobs School), is committed to providing equitable access to individuals with disabilities, including but not limited to physical access to programs and reasonable accommodations for members of the University community as outlined in the University’s Reasonable Accommodation Policy Statement.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The priority due date for receipt of the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) is March 1 each year.  Forms received after the deadline are subject to funds available.  Financial aid requests are considered after admission.  Awards are made based on need.  In most requests, parental income information is required regardless of dependency status.  A limited number of scholarships based on financial need and academic merit are provided each year.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: We encourage students to be well rounded in coursework completed, both science and non-science courses regardless of the student's major.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: We do not have a limit.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
To achieve diversity in medical admissions the Jacobs School employs a mission- aligned selection process. Mission-aligned review provides a means to tailor the individualized assessment of an applicant's capabilities through balanced consideration of life experiences, attributes, and academic metrics that when considered in combination, predict how the individual might contribute value as a medical student and physician.

Our admissions process is highly selective and it is important you make a good first impression with your application and supporting documents. We select students who thrive in collaborative settings and we expect you to work well in a collegial, supportive, and team-oriented environment.

If you are a candidate who is reapplying, you can expect to receive the same careful consideration we give to first-time applicants.  

We accept students without regard to race, sex, creed, national origin, age, sexual preference or disability.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Shadowing physicians in a clinical setting is highly recommended, as it offers the applicant a window into the work life of a physician and offers the applicant confirmation that this is the correct path forward for them.  Scribing is also acceptable.
